extracted.intended_audience: members of the scientific community and the public who detect or want to report possible research misconduct; journal editors/publishers and meeting organizers seeking consultancy or talks
extracted.subtask_description: An 'About' page / biosketch for a science-integrity investigator (Elisabeth Bik) that includes guidance for members of the public on how to report suspected plagiarism or problematic images and describes the author's consultancy, speaking availability, and conflicts/disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to report suspected plagiarism or duplicated images
rubrics_metrics.description: If you suspect plagiarism, here is a guide to some tools to use. If you see a paper with potentially duplicated images, poorly analyzed data, shoddy methods, conflict of interest, etc., do not send it to me, but please post it on PubPeer. I have written a page on how to post your concerns there. I also encourage you to write your concerns to the Editor in Chief of the journal in which the paper was published. I have written a How To page on how to do that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to a tools guide, a how-to post-on-PubPeer page, and a how-to-write-to-the-Editor page are provided. The page explicitly asks readers not to send individual suspected papers directly to the author due to volume; instead follow the linked self-help/reporting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for volunteer reporters / response policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the overwhelming amount of requests in the past, I will most likely not be able to respond to requests to help. But I have written a couple of How To guides so you can help me by doing the work yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an expectation that individual reports will usually not receive a direct response and directs users to self-service guidance. This is a procedural standard for members of the public who find problematic papers: use the guides and community reporting channels rather than expecting personal assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and conditions for consultancy and speaking engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Although almost all of the work I tweet and post about is without compensation, I am also available as a research integrity consultant to investigate specific allegations of misconduct for research institutions and scientific publishers or to give a second opinion. I will honor any request for confidentiality. I’d also be very happy to give a (virtual or in-person) seminar on my work as a research integrity volunteer, or on science misconduct in general. I ask for a speaker’s honorarium to cover my time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies services offered (investigations, second opinions, seminars), confidentiality policy for consulting cases, expectation of honorarium for talks, and provides an email address for contact. Implies paid work is carried out under confidentiality agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and disclosure practices (2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a science integrity consultant, I regularly do paid consultancy work – since 2019 – for several scientific publishers and research institutions around the world. Almost all these consulting cases are done under confidentiality agreements, so I cannot disclose the details about my clients or the cases I have investigated. Since 2019, I have received speaker fees for giving talks at several universities and institutions. From 2021-2024, I was a member of the eLife Ethics Committee, for which I received an annual stipend. From 2024 on, I am a Stanford Metric affiliate (unpaid position, but comes with access to Stanford Library and other university tools). I get free access to ImageTwin, Proofig, and iThenticate. I do not own stocks or stock options from my previous employers, uBiome or Astarte Medical. I am an author on several uBiome (later: Psomagen) patents. I have no financial or financial security ties (no stock options, no longs/short positions) to pharmaceutical, biotech companies, or charitable foundations. I do have a Patreon account, and that does generate income for me. It is not tied to specific requests to investigate particular papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full list of disclosed ties, payments, affiliations, tool access, and negative disclosures (what she does not hold). Notes that confidentiality agreements limit disclosure of client details. This constitutes a model of transparent self-disclosure about potential conflicts for a research-integrity practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool access for image forensics
rubrics_metrics.description: I get free access to ImageTwin, Proofig, and iThenticate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly names the image- and text-comparison tools the author uses/have access to; implies reliance on both manual visual screening and specialized software for detecting duplication/manipulation and plagiarism.
